title.narrative: Phase 2 - Arab region programme on good land governance in support to inclusive development, gender equality, peace and stability, and climate resilience

description.narrative:
The second phase of the “Arab Region Programme on Good Land Governance in Support to Inclusive Development, Gender Equality, Peace and Stability, and Climate Resilience” has a duration of 5 years, starting in July 2023, and a budget of USD 3.8 million. The programme’s implementation is led by the Secretariat of the Arab Land Initiative located within the Land, Housing, and Shelter Section of UN-Habitat / GLTN in close collaboration and with the guidance of the UN-Habitat Regional Office for Arab States. The project is regional in scope, with a limited number of activities to be implemented in priority countries to be identified during its inception phase. Based on the work and the lessons learnt during the first phase of the regional programme, the second phase of the Arab states good land governance programme builds on, consolidates, and expands the results achieved in the first phase of the project, which ended in December 2022. In terms of sustainability, there is the hope that, by the end of Phase 2, there will be sufficient knowledge and capacity among the land actors in the region to allow the regional work to be taken forward by regional institutions. Similarly, it is expected that national institutions and organisations will be able to shoulder the work at country level, with limited support from the international community. Ensuring good land governance and improved land administration in the Arab region is crucial for the achievement of high priority peace and development goals, which define the thematic focus of the programme: good land governance in relation to climate change (mitigation and adaptation, focusing on sustainable land management); human rights, gender equality and women’s land rights as a key avenue towards empowerment and a better standard of living; sustainable development, poverty alleviation and food security; peace and stability and the protection of housing, land and property rights for displaced people and migrants. This is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (particularly 1, 2, 5, 11, 15 and 16) and with the Voluntary Guidelines on the Responsible Governance of Tenure of Land, Fisheries and Forests in the Context of National Food Security. The programme is set to achieve a positive impact on good land governance and improved land administration through the programme’s objective: empowering and improving the capacity of regional and national stakeholders in managing and administering urban, peri-urban and rural land in the Arab states to achieve inclusive socioeconomic development, promote gender equality, foster peace and stability, and adapt to and mitigate climate change. Only an empowered, capacitated and well-connected network of local, national and regional champions will be able to sustain a long term engagement and make a positive change in the complex land governance dynamics in the Arab region, its countries and communities, with the support of the international community. Such champions are empowered and capacitated through the programme’s activities, including research, conferences, enhanced educational curricula, expert group meetings, webinars, round-table discussions, training, international exposure, providing and generating information and knowledge, and the provision support to land-related processes they own and lead. The work started in Phase 1 on coordination and collaboration, knowledge management and capacity development will be continued and further expanded, building on the partnership forged and the materials developed in the past years. The support to country level engagement will be scaled up regionally, and particular focus will be placed on three priority countries to be identified in the inception phase of the programme in collaboration with key partners.
The programme activities will revolve around four outcomes: Outcome 1: Coordination and collaboration - Land interventions are increasingly aligned and coordinated and there is improved collaboration among the land stakeholders in the region Outcome 2: Knowledge - There is more and better shared knowledge on land in the region Outcome 3: Capacity development - Individuals and institutions in the Arab region have improved capacity on land governance and land administration Outcome 4: Country level interventions - Nationally led land interventions in selected countries are catalysed, facilitated and supported through human rights-based, gender- responsive, fit-for-purpose and inclusive land tools and approaches Outcome 5: Knowledge management contribution to the Arab Land Initiative and to the Arab region programme on good land governance in support to inclusive development, gender equality, peace and stability, and climate resilience Phase 2
